title_en: Shanghai Jing'an District People's Procuratorate v. Huang Chunhai — helping criminals evade punishment and selling goods with counterfeit registered trademarks
ruling_gist_en: 1. According to the Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Application of the Subject of the Crime of Dereliction of Duty in Chapter IX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, persons who perform public duties in organizations that exercise state administrative powers in accordance with laws or regulations, or persons who perform public duties in organizations entrusted by state organs to exercise powers on behalf of state organs, or persons who, although not included in the establishment of state organs, perform public duties in state organs, shall, if they engage in dereliction of duty while exercising state powers and such conduct constitutes a crime, be investigated for criminal liability in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Law on crimes of dereliction of duty. The Tobacco Monopoly Bureau is an organization that, by being entrusted by relevant state administrative organs, exercises administrative law enforcement powers such as market inspection of tobacco monopolies and investigation and punishment of violations of tobacco monopoly regulations on behalf of the relevant state organs. Therefore, if staff members of the Tobacco Monopoly Bureau engage in dereliction of duty while exercising state powers and such conduct constitutes a crime, they shall be investigated for criminal liability in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Law on crimes of dereliction of duty.

full_text_en:
**Shanghai Jing'an District People's Procuratorate v. Huang Chunhai — case of aiding a criminal to evade punishment and selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark**

**【Ruling Summary】**

I. According to the "Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Application of the Subjects of Crimes of Dereliction of Duty in Chapter IX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China," persons who perform public duties in an organization that exercises state administrative powers in accordance with laws and regulations, persons who perform public duties in an organization entrusted by a state organ to exercise powers on its behalf, or persons who, although not included in the staffing of a state organ, perform public duties in a state organ, who, when exercising powers on behalf of the state organ, engage in dereliction of duty that constitutes a crime, shall be investigated for criminal responsibility according to the provisions of the Criminal Law on crimes of dereliction of duty. A tobacco monopoly bureau is an organization entrusted by relevant state administrative organs to exercise administrative law enforcement powers, such as inspecting the tobacco monopoly market and investigating and punishing violations of tobacco monopoly regulations, on behalf of the relevant state organs. Therefore, when a staff member of a tobacco monopoly bureau, in the course of exercising powers on behalf of the state organ, engages in dereliction of duty that constitutes a crime, they shall be investigated for criminal responsibility according to the provisions of the Criminal Law on crimes of dereliction of duty.

II. According to Article 417 of the Criminal Law, the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment refers to the act of a state organ staff member who has the duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities tipping off criminals, providing them with convenience, and helping them evade punishment. The "duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities" stipulated in this Article refers not only to the duties of criminal investigation, prosecution, adjudication, and execution of sentences legally borne by judicial organs, but also includes the duties of investigating and suppressing criminal activities conferred upon relevant administrative organs by law. The tobacco monopoly bureau, entrusted by relevant state administrative organs, exercises administrative law enforcement powers, such as inspecting the tobacco monopoly market and investigating and punishing violations of tobacco monopoly regulations, on behalf of the relevant state organs. According to Article 29 of the "Procedural Regulations for Tobacco Monopoly Administrative Penalties" of the State Tobacco Monopoly Administration, when it is discovered that an illegal act violating tobacco monopoly regulations constitutes a crime, the relevant staff member shall, according to law, transfer the case to a judicial organ for handling. Accordingly, the tobacco monopoly bureau and its staff members have the duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities that violate the tobacco monopoly. If, in the course of performing their duties, staff members of an inspection detachment of a tobacco monopoly bureau use methods such as tipping off, repeatedly revealing the arrangements and deployments of surprise inspections of counterfeit cigarette sales to criminals selling counterfeit cigarettes, thereby enabling the criminals to evade criminal punishment, they constitute the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment.

**Prosecuting Authority:** Shanghai Jing'an District People's Procuratorate.

**Defendant:** Huang Chunhai, male, 26 years old, formerly an inspector of the Inspection Detachment of the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, residing at Baotou Road, Shanghai. He was placed under bail pending trial on November 9, 2007, and arrested on March 24, 2008, for suspected crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark.

The Shanghai Jing'an District People's Procuratorate instituted a public prosecution against the Defendant Huang Chunhai for the crimes of aiding a criminal to evade punishment and selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark, before the Shanghai Jing'an District People's Court.

The Indictment alleged: During the period from September 2006 to October 2007, while serving as an inspector for the Inspection Detachment of the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch (hereinafter referred to as the Inspection Detachment), the Defendant Huang Chunhai, in the course of performing his duties to investigate and suppress the sale of counterfeit cigarettes, repeatedly used the method of tipping off, disclosing in advance the deployment arrangements of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspections of counterfeit cigarette sales to Cai Qingde (separately handled and already sentenced), the operator of the Green-Green Grocery at No. 479 Jiaozhou Road, Shanghai, which was within his jurisdiction, thereby enabling Cai Qingde to evade punishment for his criminal acts of selling counterfeit tobacco products. Furthermore, starting from November 2004, Huang Chunhai, in collusion with Cai Qingde, sold a total of over 200 cartons of counterfeit Zhonghua cigarettes to Huang Chunhai's relatives and friends, Mao Yingmei, Zhang Yuan, and others, with a total sales amount of over RMB 86,000. In summary, Huang Chunhai's actions violated Article 417 and Article 214 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law), constituting the crimes of aiding a criminal to evade punishment and selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark, and criminal responsibility should be investigated according to law.

The Defendant Huang Chunhai had no objection to the facts alleged in the indictment. His defense counsel argued that Huang Chunhai's actions did not constitute the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment, and he should only be convicted of the single crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark. The main reasons were: First, as an inspector of the Inspection Detachment, Huang Chunhai only had administrative law enforcement powers and did not have the duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities; Second, Huang Chunhai and Cai Qingde jointly sold counterfeit registered trademark cigarettes and were accomplices in the crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark. Huang Chunhai's purpose in tipping off Cai Qingde was not to help Cai Qingde evade punishment, but to help himself escape punishment. Additionally, Huang Chunhai had the circumstance of voluntary surrender, and could be given a lighter punishment according to law.

The Shanghai Jing'an District People's Court found the following facts in the first instance trial:

During the period from September 2006 to October 2007, while serving as an inspector of the Inspection Detachment, the Defendant Huang Chunhai, in the course of investigating and suppressing illegal and criminal activities involving the sale of counterfeit and inferior cigarettes, repeatedly disclosed the deployment arrangements of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspections in advance to Cai Qingde, the operator of the Green-Green Grocery at No. 479 Jiaozhou Road, Shanghai, which was within his jurisdiction. During the 2007 Spring Festival, before leaving Shanghai for private reasons, Huang Chunhai also instructed his colleague Teng Haijun (separately handled) to disclose the deployment arrangements of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspections during the Spring Festival to Cai Qingde in advance. Due to Huang Chunhai's advance tips, Cai Qingde's criminal acts of selling counterfeit registered trademark cigarettes repeatedly evaded inspection and punishment.

Separately, starting from November 2004, the Defendant Huang Chunhai repeatedly introduced others to Cai Qingde to purchase counterfeit registered trademark Zhonghua cigarettes, and then shared the profits with Cai Qingde. Through the above method, Huang Chunhai, in collusion with Cai Qingde, sold a total of over 200 cartons of counterfeit registered trademark Zhonghua cigarettes to Mao Yingmei, Zhang Yuan, and others, with a total sales amount of over RMB 86,000.

On November 7, 2007, when his work unit was investigating him, the Defendant Huang Chunhai voluntarily confessed to the above criminal facts.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence submitted by the prosecuting authority to the court and cross-examined during the trial:

1. The Institution Legal Person Certificate of the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, proving that although the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch is an institutional organization, it is entrusted by relevant state organs to be responsible for the inspection of the tobacco monopoly market within its jurisdiction and to investigate and punish violations of the tobacco monopoly.

2. The position certificate, employment letter, and law enforcement certificate for the Defendant Huang Chunhai issued by the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, proving that Huang Chunhai was an inspector of the Inspection Detachment before the incident.

3. The market inspection record sheets and overtime approval forms of the Inspection Detachment issued by the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, and the call records of the Defendant Huang Chunhai’s mobile phone, proving that the Inspection Detachment conducted multiple surprise inspections between September 2006 and October 2007, and that Huang Chunhai's mobile phone had call records with the Green-Green Grocery multiple times before the surprise inspections.

4. The testimony of Teng Haijun, proving that during the 2007 Spring Festival, before leaving Shanghai, the Defendant Huang Chunhai asked him to inform Cai Qingde of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspections in advance; and that he had informed Cai Qingde of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspections several times in advance.

5. The testimony of witness Yang Fengying, Cai Qingde's wife, proving that between September 2006 and October 2007, the Defendant Huang Chunhai and Teng Haijun repeatedly called Cai Qingde in advance to inform him of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspections, and that Cai Qingde accordingly stopped selling counterfeit registered trademark tobacco products during the surprise inspections.

6. The confession of Cai Qingde, which, in addition to corroborating the testimony of his wife Yang Fengying, also proved that from November 2004 onwards, he and the Defendant Huang Chunhai sold over 200 cartons of counterfeit registered trademark Zhonghua cigarettes to Huang Chunhai's relatives Mao Yingmei, Zhang Yuan, and others, with a total sales amount of over RMB 86,000, and that he and Huang Chunhai shared the profits.

7. The testimonies of witnesses Mao Yingmei, Zhang Yuan, Guo Dahai, Liu Yuyan, Shi Zhenbing, Shen Enfeng, and others, proving that the Defendant Huang Chunhai sold them over 200 cartons of counterfeit registered trademark Zhonghua cigarettes.

8. The testimony of witness Chen Honglin, the head of the Inspection Detachment, proving that on November 7, 2007, when the work unit was investigating him, the Defendant Huang Chunhai voluntarily confessed to the facts of informing Cai Qingde of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspection arrangements, and to jointly selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark with Cai Qingde. On the same day, he provided a written confession to the unit, and the content of his confession corroborated the witness testimonies.

The disputed focus of this case is: whether the Defendant Huang Chunhai's act of informing Cai Qingde of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspection arrangements constitutes the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment, and whether it should be punished for multiple crimes.

The Shanghai Jing'an District People's Court held in the first instance:

As an inspector of the Inspection Detachment, during his official duties of investigating and suppressing the illegal and criminal activities of selling counterfeit and inferior cigarettes, the Defendant Huang Chunhai repeatedly personally, or instructed others, to inform criminals in advance of the circumstances of surprise inspections, thereby helping criminals evade punishment. He also, in collusion with others, sold counterfeit registered trademark cigarette products in a relatively large amount. His actions constituted the crimes of aiding a criminal to evade punishment and selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark, and he should be punished according to the principle of joinder of punishments for multiple crimes. The facts of the crime alleged by the prosecuting authority were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the legal characterization was correct.

I. The Defendant Huang Chunhai met the subject qualifications for the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment.

Firstly, the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, is an organization legally established to manage the tobacco monopoly market within its jurisdiction. Although it is an institutional organization, it is entrusted by relevant state administrative organs to exercise administrative law enforcement powers such as inspecting the tobacco monopoly market within its jurisdiction and investigating and punishing violations of the tobacco monopoly. According to Article 18, Paragraph 1, and Article 19, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the "Administrative Penalties Law of the People's Republic of China," administrative organs may, in accordance with laws, regulations, or rules, delegate, within their statutory authority, the implementation of administrative penalties to organizations legally established to manage public affairs. Based on the above provisions and in conjunction with the Institution Legal Person Certificate of the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, it can be confirmed that the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, is an organization entrusted by relevant state administrative organs to exercise administrative law enforcement powers, such as inspecting the tobacco monopoly market and investigating and punishing violations of tobacco monopoly regulations, on behalf of the relevant state organs. According to the "Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Application of the Subjects of Crimes of Dereliction of Duty in Chapter IX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China," persons who perform public duties in an organization that exercises state administrative powers in accordance with laws and regulations, persons who perform public duties in an organization entrusted by a state organ to exercise powers on its behalf, or persons who, although not included in the staffing of a state organ, perform public duties in a state organ, who, when exercising powers on behalf of the state organ, engage in dereliction of duty that constitutes a crime, shall be investigated for criminal responsibility according to the provisions of the Criminal Law on crimes of dereliction of duty. In this case, the Defendant Huang Chunhai was an inspector of the Inspection Detachment. His Inspection Detachment was affiliated with the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, and was specifically responsible for the inspection of the tobacco monopoly market within the jurisdiction and the investigation and punishment of violations of the tobacco monopoly. Therefore, it can be determined that Huang Chunhai was a person who performed public duties in an organization entrusted by a state organ to exercise powers on its behalf. When exercising powers on behalf of the state organ, he should be considered a "state organ staff member."

Secondly, according to Article 417 of the Criminal Law, the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment refers to the act of a state organ staff member who has the duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities tipping off criminals, providing them with convenience, and helping them evade punishment. The "duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities" stipulated in this Article refers not only to the duties of criminal investigation, prosecution, adjudication, and execution of sentences legally borne by judicial organs, but also includes the duties of investigating and suppressing criminal activities conferred upon relevant administrative organs by law. Article 402 of the Criminal Law stipulates: "Any administrative law enforcement personnel who, engaging in malpractices for personal gain, fails to transfer a case that should be transferred to a judicial organ for investigation of criminal responsibility according to law, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention; if the consequences are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years." The "Regulations on the Transfer of Suspected Criminal Cases by Administrative Law Enforcement Organs" promulgated by the State Council also clearly stipulates: "Any administrative law enforcement personnel who, engaging in malpractices for personal gain, fails to transfer a case that should be transferred to a judicial organ for investigation of criminal responsibility, if the circumstances are serious, shall be investigated for criminal responsibility." Accordingly, when administrative organs discover suspected crimes in the course of administrative law enforcement, they shall transfer the case to a judicial organ for investigation of criminal responsibility according to law. This is the statutory duty of administrative organs to investigate and suppress criminal activities. The "Provisions of the Supreme People's Procuratorate on the Standards for Filing Cases of Crimes of Dereliction of Duty and Infringement of Rights" also clearly stipulates that the subject of the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment is "judicial and public security, national security, customs, taxation, and other state organ staff members who have the duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities." In this case, the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, was entrusted by relevant state administrative organs to exercise administrative law enforcement powers, such as inspecting the tobacco monopoly market and investigating and punishing violations of tobacco monopoly regulations, on behalf of the relevant state organs. The Inspection Detachment to which the Defendant Huang Chunhai belonged was affiliated with the Shanghai Tobacco Monopoly Bureau, Jing'an Branch, and was specifically responsible for the inspection of the tobacco monopoly market within the jurisdiction and the investigation and punishment of violations of the tobacco monopoly. According to Article 29 of the "Procedural Regulations for Tobacco Monopoly Administrative Penalties" of the State Tobacco Monopoly Administration, when it is discovered that an illegal act violating tobacco monopoly regulations constitutes a crime, the relevant staff member shall, according to law, collect and organize the relevant evidence and transfer the case to a judicial organ for handling. Accordingly, staff of the tobacco monopoly bureau, upon discovering criminal activities, must collect and organize relevant evidence and transfer the case to a judicial organ for handling. This constitutes the duty of the tobacco monopoly bureau and its staff to investigate and suppress criminal activities. As an inspector of the Inspection Detachment, Huang Chunhai bore this duty.

In summary, the defense counsel's argument that the Defendant Huang Chunhai did not meet the subject qualifications for the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment could not be established and was not adopted.

II. The Defendant Huang Chunhai committed the criminal act of aiding a criminal to evade punishment.

According to the facts of this case, while serving as an inspector of the Inspection Detachment, the Defendant Huang Chunhai repeatedly disclosed the deployment arrangements of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspections in advance to Cai Qingde, thereby enabling Cai Qingde's criminal acts of selling counterfeit registered trademark cigarettes to repeatedly evade inspection and punishment. The above actions of Huang Chunhai constituted the criminal act of aiding a criminal to evade punishment.

III. The conduct of the Defendant Huang Chunhai should be punished for multiple crimes: the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment and the crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark.

The Defendant Huang Chunhai repeatedly introduced others to Cai Qingde to purchase a total of over 200 cartons of counterfeit registered trademark Zhonghua cigarettes, with a total sales amount of over RMB 86,000, and then shared the profits with Cai Qingde. The above actions of Huang Chunhai constituted the joint criminal act of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark.

Although the Defendant Huang Chunhai and Cai Qingde jointly sold counterfeit registered trademark Zhonghua cigarettes, this does not affect the fact that his act of tipping off Cai Qingde constituted the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment. Huang Chunhai's tipping off of Cai Qingde certainly had the subjective purpose of preventing his own crimes from being exposed, but this does not negate that he also had the purpose of helping Cai Qingde evade criminal punishment. The defense counsel's argument that "Huang Chunhai's purpose in tipping off Cai Qingde was only to escape punishment himself, and therefore he should only be convicted of the single crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark" could not be established and was not adopted.

In summary, the Defendant Huang Chunhai, as an inspector of the Inspection Detachment, had the duty to investigate and suppress the crime of selling counterfeit registered trademark cigarette products. However, he colluded with a criminal selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark, jointly committed the crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark, and tipped off the criminal to help him evade punishment. His actions constituted the crimes of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark and aiding a criminal to evade punishment, for which he should be punished according to the joinder of punishments for multiple crimes. Huang Chunhai voluntarily confessed to all his criminal facts when his work unit was investigating him, which could be considered as voluntary surrender, and could be given a lighter punishment according to law. The defense counsel's opinion that Huang Chunhai had the circumstance of voluntary surrender and could be given a lighter punishment according to law should be adopted. Huang Chunhai and Cai Qingde played essentially similar roles in the joint crime, with no distinction between principal and accessory, and both should be punished according to law. Accordingly, in accordance with Articles 417, 214, Paragraph 1 of Article 25, Paragraphs 1 and 4 of Article 26, Paragraph 1 of Article 67, Article 69, and Article 64 of the Criminal Law, and the "Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Application of the Subjects of Crimes of Dereliction of Duty in Chapter IX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China," the Shanghai Jing'an District People's Court rendered the following judgment on June 6, 2008:

I. The Defendant Huang Chunhai is found guilty of the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment and is sentenced to one year and six months of fixed-term imprisonment; guilty of the crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark and is sentenced to one year of fixed-term imprisonment and a fine of RMB 2,000; the combined sentence is two years of fixed-term imprisonment and a fine of RMB 2,000.

II. The illegal gains of the Defendant Huang Chunhai shall be recovered and turned over to the State Treasury.

Huang Chunhai, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, arguing: The Appellant Huang Chunhai did not have the duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities. Huang Chunhai jointly sold counterfeit registered trademark cigarettes with Cai Qingde, and his purpose in tipping off Cai Qingde was solely to escape punishment himself. Therefore, Huang Chunhai was merely an accomplice in the crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark and did not constitute the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment. The legal characterization in the first-instance judgment was incorrect, and the sentence was too heavy, requesting a reversal and amendment according to law.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found by the first-instance court.

The disputed focus in the second instance remained: whether the Defendant Huang Chunhai's act of informing Cai Qingde of the Inspection Detachment's surprise inspection arrangements constituted the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment, and whether it should be punished for multiple crimes.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

The Appellant Huang Chunhai, as an inspector of the Inspection Detachment, was, according to the "Tobacco Monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China," the "Administrative Penalties Law of the People's Republic of China," and the specific functional provisions of his department, obligated to investigate and punish illegal activities such as scalping tobacco monopoly products, producing and selling counterfeit registered trademark tobacco products, and, for related illegal activities that constituted crimes, had the duty to transfer the cases to judicial organs for investigation of criminal responsibility according to law. Therefore, Huang Chunhai met the subject requirements for the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment, and his appeal argument that he did not have the duty to investigate and suppress criminal activities could not be established. Huang Chunhai tipped off Cai Qingde, helping Cai Qingde evade criminal punishment, and his actions constituted the crime of aiding a criminal to evade punishment.

The Appellant Huang Chunhai introduced others to Cai Qingde to purchase counterfeit registered trademark cigarettes and shared the profits with Cai Qingde, involving a relatively large amount. His actions constituted the crime of selling goods bearing a counterfeit registered trademark.

In summary, the Appellant Huang Chunhai committed two crimes: the crime of assisting criminals to evade punishment and the crime of selling counterfeit registered trademark goods, and shall be punished for multiple crimes in accordance with law. The facts found by the court of first instance are clear, the evidence is credible and sufficient, the conviction and sentencing are appropriate, and the trial procedures are lawful. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court ruled on September 17, 2008, as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
